title: The Mechanism of Ultrasonic Lysis of Enterococcus faecium F11.1G in Repairing LPS-Induced Inflammatory Damage in IECs via RNA-seq and LC-MS.
authors: Bai, Tiantian; Zhang, Yanlong; E, Guangxu; Zhang, Meng; Guo, Xuefeng; Liu, Junfeng
one_liner_zh: 该文研究超声波裂解粪肠球菌对LPS诱导肠上皮细胞炎症的修复机制，基于转录组和代谢组分析，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced damage to the intestinal epithelial barrier leads to gut inflammation, and intracellular metabolites of lactic acid bacteria may participate in regulating this process to exert probiotic effects. This study aimed to investigate the repair effects and molecular mechanisms of ultrasonic disruption-treated Enterococcus faecium F11.1G (F11.1G) on the model (primary lamb IECs + 5 mug/mL LPS for 6 h). Then, results demonstrated that 10(8) CFU/mL F11.1G significantly suppressed the excessive secretion of pro-inflammatory factors (IL-6, IL-8, IL-1beta, TNF-alpha) induced by LPS. Gene Ontology (GO) analysis revealed that differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were primarily enriched in cellular response to lipopolysaccharide, inflammatory response, and canonical NF-kappaB signaling pathways. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analysis showed enrichment in NF-kappaB signaling pathway and MAPK signaling pathway. PPI network identified key genes including IL-1beta, TNF, IL-8, RELB, FOS, TNFAIP3, NFKBIA, and MMP9. KEGG analysis indicated differentially abundant metabolites (DAMs) enrichment in purine metabolism and the endocannabinoid system. Spearman correlation analysis revealed positive correlations between pro-inflammatory genes and endogenous protective metabolites, such as adenosine and PEA, while showing negative correlations with multiple purine metabolites. Correlational analysis indicates that F11.1G alleviates intestinal inflammatory damage primarily by suppressing NF-kappaB/MAPK pathway activation and may synergistically regulate purine and endocannabinoid metabolism.
abstract_zh: 脂多糖（LPS）诱导的肠道上皮屏障损伤导致肠道炎症，而乳酸菌的胞内代谢物可能参与调控该过程以发挥益生作用。本研究旨在探讨经超声破碎处理的屎肠球菌F11.1G（F11.1G）对模型（原代羔羊肠上皮细胞 + 5 μg/mL LPS处理6小时）的修复效果及其分子机制。结果表明，10^8 CFU/mL F11.1G显著抑制了LPS诱导的促炎因子（IL-6、IL-8、IL-1β、TNF-α）的过度分泌。基因本体论（Gene Ontology, GO）分析显示，差异表达基因（differentially expressed genes, DEGs）主要富集于对脂多糖的细胞反应、炎症反应及经典NF-κB信号通路。京都基因与基因组百科全书（Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes, KEGG）分析显示富集于NF-κB信号通路和MAPK信号通路。蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络鉴定了关键基因，包括IL-1β、TNF、IL-8、RELB、FOS、TNFAIP3、NFKBIA和MMP9。KEGG分析显示差异丰度代谢物（differentially abundant metabolites, DAMs）富集于嘌呤代谢和内源性大麻素系统。Spearman相关性分析显示，促炎基因与内源性保护性代谢物（如腺苷和PEA）呈正相关，而与多种嘌呤代谢物呈负相关。相关性分析表明，F11.1G主要通过抑制NF-κB/MAPK通路激活来缓解肠道炎症损伤，并可能协同调节嘌呤和内源性大麻素代谢。
